properties.note: Athens and the surrounding Attic peninsula.
The region of Thebes, Orchomenus and Plataea.
The island region, including Chalcis and Eretria.
The small region of Megara between Attica and Corinthia.
The region around Parnassus; Delphi had a distinct sacred and political status.
The small inland Dorian district of central Greece, distinct from Doris in Asia Minor.
Western Locris, on the north coast of the Corinthian Gulf.
Eastern Locrian district around Opus.
The Locrian district near Mount Cnemis and Thermopylae.
The district at the head of the Malian Gulf.
Two neighboring Classical districts in the Spercheios valley and Oeta highlands, shown together at this map scale.
The upland district southwest of the Thessalian plain.
A broad geographical outline including the northern uplands around Aperantia; not the extent of the later Aetolian League.
The region west of the lower Achelous River.
The Thessalian plain and surrounding districts are grouped here; internal tetrads are not separately demarcated.
The coastal district along Ossa and Pelion, adjoining Thessaly.
A broad geographical region; Chaonia, Thesprotia, Molossis and neighboring uplands are grouped, not separate state boundaries.
A broad regional outline. Macedonian territory expanded during the Classical period; this is not a map of the kingdom at a single date or of Alexander’s empire.
The three peninsulas and their hinterland, shown as a geographical region rather than a political league.
The northern Peloponnesian coastal region, not the later extent of the Achaean League.
The central Peloponnesian highlands.
Western Peloponnese, including Triphylia in this generalized outline; control of its southern districts was contested.
The southwestern Peloponnese. A geographical region both before and after its liberation from Spartan control in 369 BCE.
The region of Sparta. Cynuria is included following its usual Classical association with Laconia; the Argive-Spartan frontier was disputed.
The northeastern Peloponnesian region around Argos; its borders with Corinthia and Laconia varied.
The territory around Corinth and the Isthmus.
The island as a geographical region, containing many independent Classical communities.
The Ionian coastal region, with Chios and Samos. Tint indicates a regional association, not continuous political control.
The Aeolian coastal region and Lesbos, grouped by regional association.
The southwest Asian Dorian region, with Cos and Rhodes. This is an ethnic-geographical grouping, not the membership of a league at every Classical date.
The region around Troy, included for the wider Classical Greek reading area.
The peninsula along the European side of the Hellespont.
